claims.claim: Under normalized nonnegative effective weights, the harmonic common-mode snapshot efficiency equals the squared magnitude of the weighted delay phasor and admits the exact pairwise cosine-loss identity.
The modeled alignment efficiency lies in [0,1].
The alignment loss is at most omega squared times the weighted delay variance.
Var_w(tau) <= (1-q)/Omega^2 is sufficient for eta >= q for every modeled mode with |omega| <= Omega.
Equal delays, a static mode, or one active channel retain eta=1; two equal channels half a cycle apart have eta=0.
The delay-variance budget is sufficient rather than necessary because a full-period delay can have eta=1 at large raw delay variance.
